vcard_page.heading: What is a vCard?
vcard_page.intro: A vCard is a digital business card. It holds contact details such as name, phone number, email address, company, and address. As a file it uses the .vcf extension. When you open it, the phone or computer recognises the data and offers to save the contact in the address book.
vcard_page.why_text: A vCard lets you pass on contact details quickly and completely. Nobody has to type names, phone numbers, or email addresses by hand. That saves time and avoids typos.
vcard_page.spread_text: vCard is a widespread standard that has been around since the 1990s. iPhone, Android, Apple Contacts, Google Contacts, Outlook, and Thunderbird can open and import .vcf files. Version 3.0, which this tool uses, is read reliably by current devices.
vcard_page.fields_heading: What data does a vCard hold?
vcard_page.fields_text: A vCard holds at least a name. You can also store phone numbers, email addresses, company, job title, postal address, and website. Which fields you include is up to you.
vcard_page.qr_heading: How does a vCard work as a QR code?
vcard_page.qr_text: The contact details in a vCard can sit directly in a QR code. When you scan it, the phone reads the data and offers to create a new contact. No extra app or website visit is needed.

business_card_page.heading: Create a QR Code for Your Business Card
business_card_page.intro_p1: A business card QR code turns a printed card into a direct path to the address book. With this generator, your contact details are stored as a vCard directly inside the QR code. When someone scans it on iPhone or Android, they can save the contact without typing your name, phone number or email address by hand.
business_card_page.intro_p2: The code works without a redirect, without an account and without an expiry date. The details you enter stay local in your browser and are not sent to a server. That makes a QR code for business cards useful in print, because the scan can work even when no internet connection is available. If your phone number, email address or company changes later, create a new code and replace it in the next print file.
business_card_page.vcard_heading: vCard QR Code Instead of a Website Link
business_card_page.vcard_text: A URL QR code opens a web page, such as a profile or landing page. A vCard QR code for a business card contains the contact details themselves. After the scan, the phone recognises the digital business card and offers to save it as a new contact. For networking, trade shows and client meetings, this is often faster than sending people through a browser first. A website link can be useful when you need editable content, but for plain contact details the vCard route is more direct and does not depend on hosting, tracking parameters or a mobile web page.
business_card_page.fields_heading: Which Contact Details Belong in the QR Code?
business_card_page.fields_intro: A business card QR code generator should include only the details that are useful after a scan. Too much data makes the pattern finer and can reduce scan reliability in print. In most cases, include:
business_card_page.size_heading: How Large Should the QR Code Be on a Business Card?
business_card_page.size_text: For a QR code on a business card, we recommend at least about 2.5 × 2.5 cm. A vCard holds more characters than a short web address, so the code should not be placed too small. Leave enough clear space around it, often called the quiet zone, and always test the final print size with more than one phone. If many fields are filled in, the QR pattern becomes denser. In that case, shorten optional details or make the code slightly larger in the layout.
business_card_page.format_text: For professional print files, SVG is usually the best choice. The vector file can be scaled cleanly in layout software without becoming blurry. PNG is useful for digital use, such as email signatures, presentations or quick drafts. If you are sending a business card to print, use the SVG file when possible.
business_card_page.placement_heading: Place the QR Code Correctly on the Business Card
business_card_page.placement_text: Use strong contrast: a dark code on a light background is the most reliable. Keep enough distance from text, logos and trim edges so the camera can recognise the QR code clearly. Avoid very light colours, transparent backgrounds and busy patterns. Before production, print a test at actual size and scan it under normal lighting. Check not only that the camera recognises the code, but also that every contact field appears correctly. Confirm phone numbers with country codes, company spelling, the website and any extra email addresses before the cards go to print.

faq.heading: vCard QR Code FAQ
faq.q1: What is a vCard QR code?
faq.a1:
A vCard QR code is a digital business card you can scan. It holds contact details such as name, phone number, email address, and company. The phone reads that data and offers to save it as a new contact.

The vCard sits in the QR code. No website opens, and no internet connection is required.
faq.q2: How do I create a QR code for my business card?
faq.a2:
First enter the contact details that should appear on the business card. Then download the QR code and scan it with your phone. Check that every field shows up correctly.

For print, use the SVG file. Place it in the layout and test the code again at the real print size.
faq.q3: Which contact details belong in the QR code?
faq.a3:
Store only details that are useful after a scan. Name, company, job title, phone number, email address, and website are usually enough. An address makes sense if it is also on the card.

Use phone numbers with a country code, for example +41 instead of 079. The more data the QR code holds, the finer its pattern becomes, and the harder it can be to scan on a small card.
faq.q4: How large should the QR code be on a business card?
faq.a4:
We recommend at least 2.5 × 2.5 cm. A vCard holds more data than a short web address, so it usually needs a slightly larger QR code.

Leave enough clear space around the code. Do not put text, images, or trim edges there. Always test the QR code at the final print size and on more than one phone.
faq.q5: Can the QR code be coloured?
faq.a5:
Yes. What matters is clear contrast: the QR code should be dark and the background light. Light colours, similar tones, or a dark background can make scanning harder.

What looks fine on screen can look weaker in print. Check a printout at full size, especially on coloured or uncoated paper.
faq.q6: Should I download SVG, PNG, or VCF?
faq.a6:
SVG works best for business cards and other print. You can scale the file up or down without losing quality.

PNG suits digital uses such as email signatures or presentations. The VCF file holds the contact without a QR code. You can open it, send it, or import it into an address book.
faq.q7: How is this different from a URL or LinkedIn QR code?
faq.a7:
A URL QR code opens a website. A LinkedIn QR code leads to a LinkedIn profile. A vCard QR code hands the contact details straight to the phone's address book.

A printed vCard cannot be updated later. If a phone number or email address changes, you need a new QR code. In return, the code works without hosting, an account, or a redirect.
faq.q8: Do you store my contact details or track scans?
faq.a8:
No. The contact details you enter are processed in your browser and are not sent to our server. The finished QR code has no tracking URL. So vcardqr.ch does not learn when or by whom it is scanned.

The site only measures anonymous page views with an analytics tool. That statistic has no contact details and no information about later scans.
faq.q9: Does the QR code work on iPhone and Android?
faq.a9:
Yes. On iPhone you can scan the QR code with the Camera app. Most Android phones also recognise it with the camera or with Google Lens. Then you can save the contact in the address book.

An extra app is usually not needed.
faq.q10: Is the vCard QR code generator free and open source?
faq.a10: Yes. The generator is free and works without an account, subscription, or watermark. The source code is published on GitHub under the MIT license.
